Get free snooker betting tips and predictions from OLBG tipsters throughout the season, covering the major tournaments, including the World Championship.

OLBG also provides betting tips for other sports, with the most popular selections across all sports on our betting tips page.
How to Use Our Snooker Betting Tips and Predictions

Each snooker tip on this page shows the selection, the share of tips backing it and the comments behind it, so you can see the reasoning before you place a bet.

To see new snooker tips as they are posted, follow tipsters with the MyTipsters feature in the OLBG App. If you'd rather compare tipsters first, our snooker tipsters page shows their records in full.

Our snooker tips are for adults aged 18 or over. They show what our tipsters think, not what will happen, and a single frame can change the result of a match. Only bet what you can afford to lose, and if gambling is causing you concern, free support is available from GamCare and GambleAware.
Snooker Betting Markets Covered by Our Tips

Our snooker predictions cover four markets: three for individual matches and one for antepost selections.

MarketWhat it coversApplies to
Win MatchWhich player wins the match.Individual matches
Handicap BettingThe match result once a frame handicap is applied, which evens up matches between players of different standards.Individual matches
Frame BettingThe final frame score of a match.Individual matches
Win TournamentWhich player wins the whole tournament, placed in advance as an antepost selection.Antepost

For a fuller explanation of how each bet type works, see our snooker betting guide.
Snooker Winning Margins and Handicap Betting Stats

The stats in this section and the two that follow cover the last ten completed editions of each Triple Crown event: the World Championship, the Masters and the UK Championship. The figures come from OLBG's own database of results and cover the main stages only, from the last 32 at the World Championship and UK Championship and from the last 16 at the Masters. Walkovers are excluded.

Match length shapes margins. Average winning margins range from 3.6 to 4.7 frames at the World Championship, where matches are longer, and from 2.5 to 3.1 frames in the best of 11 rounds at the Masters and UK Championship. A player on a -1.5 frame handicap needs to win by two or more frames, while a player on +1.5 covers by winning or losing by a single frame. A match that does not go to a deciding frame finishes by two or more frames, and 76.1% of Masters and UK Championship matches from the last 16 to the semi-finals finished that way.

Snooker Final Frame Scores and Frame Betting Stats

Frame Betting is a bet on the final score of a match, so how often each scoreline occurs is the natural starting point. The figures below use the same last ten completed editions of the World Championship, Masters and UK Championship.

Best of 11: Masters and UK Championship

From the last 16 to the semi-finals, 6-5 is the most common final score at 23.9% of matches, and 6-0 is the rarest at 3.9%. The percentages are based on 140 matches per event.

Triple Crown Snooker Winners: Last Ten Editions

Across the last ten completed editions of the World Championship, Masters and UK Championship, 30 finals have produced 14 different winners. Ronnie O'Sullivan has won seven of them, and he and Judd Trump are the only players to have won all three events in that period.

PlayerWorld ChampionshipMastersUK ChampionshipTotal titles
Ronnie O'Sullivan2237
Judd Trump1214
Mark Selby2024
Mark Allen0112
Neil Robertson0112
Kyren Wilson1102
Zhao Xintong1012

Seven other players have won one title each: Yan Bingtao, Shaun Murphy and Stuart Bingham at the Masters, Ding Junhui at the UK Championship, and Luca Brecel, Mark Williams and Wu Yize at the World Championship.

These are past results and do not predict future winners. For previews and betting angles on individual events, see our Masters and UK Championship betting guides, or the snooker blogs.
World Snooker Championship Betting Tips and Predictions

The World Snooker Championship is the final ranking event of the season and one of snooker's three Triple Crown events. It is held at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield.

We provide Win Tournament tips ahead of the event and tips on individual matches as it progresses. For the draw and form, see our World Snooker Championship preview.

This page is written by Darren Brett, who has bet on snooker for decades and manages OLBG's Tipster Competition, with editorial oversight from Steve Madgwick, OLBG's Editor-in-Chief.

About the author

Darren Brett is a Content Editor at OLBG with over 30 years' experience in racing and betting. He has managed OLBG's Tipster Competition for more than a decade, has bet on snooker for decades and writes OLBG's snooker tournament betting guides.

- Darren Brett, Content Editor

About the editor

Steve Madgwick is OLBG's Editor-in-Chief, with over 20 years' experience in journalism and the gambling industry. He oversees the editorial standards and accuracy of OLBG's betting content.

- Steve Madgwick, Editor-In-Chief

FAQ

Snooker Betting Tips FAQs

  • Yes. Snooker betting tips from OLBG tipsters are free to view on this page, along with the comments behind the selections.

  • OLBG tipsters share snooker predictions throughout the season, covering the major tournaments, including the World Championship. The tournament calendar on this page lists UK and international events, with links to our betting previews.

  • Our snooker tips cover four markets: Win Match, Handicap Betting and Frame Betting for individual matches, and Win Tournament for antepost selections. For a fuller explanation of each bet type, see our snooker betting guide.

  • Yes. We provide Win Tournament tips ahead of the World Snooker Championship and tips on individual matches as it progresses. For the draw and form, see our World Snooker Championship preview.

  • Each selection shows its market alongside the tips and comments behind it. Experts are OLBG tipsters with high strike rates or current-month or six-month profitability in snooker. Value Rating compares the odds of a selection with its theoretical chance of winning, based on the percentage of tips for it.

  • A frame handicap gives one player a head start in frames. A player on a -1.5 frame handicap needs to win by two or more frames, while the opponent on +1.5 covers by winning the match or losing by a single frame.

  • From the last 16 to the semi-finals at the Masters and UK Championship, 6-5 is the most common final score at 23.9% of matches. 6-3 and 6-2 follow at 21.1% each, and 6-0 is the rarest at 3.9%. The figures cover the last ten completed editions of each event.

  • Approved OLBG tipsters who share snooker tips can win prizes in the monthly Tipster Competition. There are two snooker tables each month: one that rewards tips with comments and one that counts all tips. Each has its own qualifying rules and prize split, shown in the competition section above and on our prizes page.
